backend/servers/api-server/src/services/document_generation.rs:535-540 — after calling self.llm_client.chat(...).await?, the code does `let content = response.choices.first().map(|c| c.message.content.clone()).unwrap_or_default();`. When the LLM returns an EMPTY `choices` array (provider returned no completion — content-filter block, truncated/streamed-away response, or a provider returning 200 with zero choices), `unwrap_or_default()` yields an empty String "" instead of erroring. The empty content is then parsed and returned as a SUCCESSFUL document generation.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/document_generation.rs:706-711 — identical pattern in the announcement-draft path: `response.choices.first().map(|c| c.message.content.clone()).unwrap_or_default()` feeds parse_announcement_drafts(&content) with "" on empty choices, so an LLM no-op silently produces zero/blank drafts reported as success rather than a retriable error.

Impact: a transient LLM failure that returns no choices is laundered into a blank document / empty draft set that looks like a valid result to the caller (and to the user who requested the generated document). Landable fix: treat an empty `choices` (or empty/whitespace content) as an explicit error return (e.g. a DocumentGenerationError::EmptyCompletion) so the request fails loudly / is retried, instead of unwrap_or_default() masking it. Note: the unwrap_or_default() calls at lines ~661 and ~773 are benign (optional audience/building-context formatting) and are NOT part of this finding.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/syndication.rs:289-406 — SyndicationService::process_syndication_job() is a SIMULATION STUB, not a real portal integration. The PUBLISH arm comment says '// Simulate publishing to portal', it mints a MOCK external id via `format!("{}_{}", payload.portal, uuid::Uuid::new_v4())` (line 316-317), and then marks the listing syndication_status = SYNCED (line 322-330). backend/servers/api-server/src/services/syndication.rs — process_syndication_job has ZERO callers in the entire backend: `grep -rn process_syndication_job backend --include=*.rs` matches only the definition. create_publish_jobs (line 108), create_status_change_jobs (line 158) and create_update_job (line 239) are called from routes/listings.rs:540,655,661 and enqueue background jobs into the SYNDICATION_QUEUE ("syndication", line 15) with max_attempts=3. But the only background-job worker loop in api-server is push_fanout.rs:1334 process_pending_jobs, which drains a DIFFERENT queue. No worker dequeues the "syndication" queue and dispatches to process_syndication_job. Net effect: when a manager marks a listing for portal syndication, jobs are persisted but NEVER processed — the listing is never published to the external portal and never even reaches SYNCED, silently, with no error surfaced to the user.

Landable fix (backend-only, api-core): (1) wire a syndication-queue worker that claims jobs from SYNDICATION_QUEUE and calls process_syndication_job, OR fold syndication dispatch into an existing job runner; and (2) replace the mock-external-id/no-HTTP body of process_syndication_job with a real portal client call (build_listing_payload + photos are already prepared). Until then the whole listing-syndication feature (Story 105.x) is wired at the UI/enqueue layer but non-functional end-to-end. Mirrors the previously-flagged voice-cmd-fabricated-success / community-wired-nonfunctional class.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/documents/intelligence.rs:814-825 — in handler `ai_summarize_document` (fn at :601) the summary persistence result is fully discarded: `let _ = state.document_repo.update_summary(id, &summary, key_points_json, None, None, Some(word_count), Some(language)).await;`. backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/documents/intelligence.rs:836-845 — immediately after the discarded write, the handler unconditionally returns `Ok(Json(AiSummarizeResponse { ... }))` (HTTP 200) with the summary. backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/documents/core.rs:2005-2017 — in the document-upload multipart handler, the `folder_id` field is read as text and parsed with `if !text.is_empty() { folder_id = text.parse::<Uuid>().ok(); }`. Systemic `!!` non-null assertions on nullable UI-state properties across the Compose androidApp: ListingDetailScreen.kt:121,125,132,149,160 (`state.errorMessage!!`, `state.listing!!` from `viewModel.state.collectAsState()`); InquiriesScreen.kt:169 (`errorMessage!!` from a local `var by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }`); FavoritesScreen.kt:164 (same pattern); AccountScreen.kt:174 (`notificationPrefs!!` inside `if (notificationsExpanded && notificationPrefs != null)`). Kotlin cannot smart-cast a property getter on `state` nor a delegated `var`, so the branch guard does not imply non-null at the use site.

The pattern is a latent crash class: while Compose's snapshot system usually keeps reads within one composition consistent, any state update between the null-check condition evaluation and the argument-list evaluation (e.g. the ViewModel's StateFlow emitting from a coroutine mid-composition, or a `LaunchedEffect` in a sibling branch mutating the local `errorMessage` state) will throw KotlinNullPointerException. This is the exact category of bug that killed VoteDetailScreen (see the neighbour segment's 2026-08-23 finding on Rules of Hooks) — silent-until-it-crashes state-management fragility.

Idiomatic fix mirrors how the same file already gates other branches: capture the value into a local val at the top of the `when` branch, e.g. `state.listing != null -> { val listing = state.listing; ... ListingContent(listing = listing, ...) }` or use `state.listing?.let { listing -> ... } ?: return`. The FavoritesScreen retry lambda demonstrates the safer style with `.fold(onSuccess = { ... })`. Applying the fix removes the `!!` and lets the compiler enforce the invariant.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/services/search_alert_drainer.rs:317-325 — after a transport send succeeds (any_ok == true), the drainer calls mark_search_alert_notified(alert.id); if that DB write returns Err it is only tracing::error!'d. backend/servers/reality-server/src/state.rs:855 — sso_sessions: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, PendingSsoSession>>>, an unbounded in-memory map initialised empty at state.rs:991. Entries are inserted on SSO initiation (routes/sso.rs:94) and removed ONLY on a successful callback lookup (routes/sso.rs:243).

The 10-minute expiry (routes/sso.rs:251-257) is enforced lazily AFTER a callback removes the entry — there is no background sweeper / retain() that proactively evicts expired PendingSsoSession rows. Any SSO flow that starts but never completes the callback (user abandons, or an attacker scripts the authorize initiation) leaves its entry resident for the whole process lifetime.

The authorize/initiation endpoint is public (SSO login start, no prior session), so an unauthenticated caller can grow the map without bound → gradual memory-exhaustion DoS across the reality-server process. Fix: sweep expired entries on insert, or move pending SSO sessions to Redis with a TTL (the crate already uses Redis for sessions per the stack docs).

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/lib/auth-context.tsx:142-149 — checkSession() (runs on every mount) treats ANY non-ok /api/v1/users/me response as a definitive auth failure: `if (meResp.ok) {...return} clearStoredSession()`. A transient 5xx (500/502/503 backend blip, gateway restart) therefore wipes the stored bearer session and logs the user out.

The sibling refreshSession() at L221-237 handles the exact same call correctly: it only calls clearStoredSession()/setUser(null) on `meResp.status === 401 || 403` and explicitly leaves 5xx as transient ('Any other status (5xx, etc.) is treated as transient'). checkSession lacks that status discrimination, so the two entry points disagree on the same server response.

Effect: a momentary reality-server hiccup at page load silently signs valid users out (and drops them to the cookie/SSO path which, per the login() comment, isn't fully shipped). Fix: gate the clearStoredSession() in checkSession on 401/403 like refreshSession does.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/inquiries/page.tsx:47-50 — handleCancel() fires `cancelInquiry.mutate(inquiry.id)` and immediately `setShowCancelConfirm(false)` with no error handling: the useCancelInquiry mutation has no onError, and the component renders no isError branch for it. A failed cancel (network error / 4xx-5xx) is swallowed — the confirm dialog closes, no toast/alert is shown, and the inquiry silently stays active while the user believes it was cancelled.
Contrast with the page's query error handling (L332 'Failed to load inquiries. Please try again.'), which does surface load failures — only the mutation path lacks equivalent feedback.

Low severity (no crash/data loss) but a real UX-correctness gap on an authenticated action. Fix: pass onError to mutate() (or read cancelInquiry.isError) and surface a retry/error message; keep the confirm open or re-open on failure.
